metadata.title: Why a Watermark Can't Tell You Who Wrote It.

skin_warnings: B00: palette=claude but the cold open is 'un-annotated' — COLD OPEN LAW wants ClaudeComposerAsk

beats.narration_text: Someone asked what Claude's new watermark actually proves. Good question — most people guess wrong. Liam. Take them through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Shannon puppet, lab, speaks to camera, hands off

beats.note: Audio is baked into media/B00.mp4 by Seedance. No mp3 for this beat.

beats.narration_text: Future Claude models leave an invisible mark in the text they write.

shot.new_visual_element: Text block, mark implied not shown

production_viz.label: Text block, mark implied not shown
production_viz.mechanic: A short paragraph of ordinary text on cream. Nothing visibly changes. A soft terracotta underline sweeps beneath it once and fades — the mark is present but never rendered as a visible artefact.

beats.narration_text: Nothing is added to it — no hidden characters, no extra cost, and nothing that points back to you.

production_viz.label: Three things crossed off
production_viz.mechanic: Three chips appear in a row and are struck through one at a time in narration order: HIDDEN CHARACTERS, EXTRA COST, YOUR IDENTITY. Strike lands on the spoken word.

beats.narration_text: Hold on to one thing while we go: a paragraph you wrote yourself, then asked Claude to fix the grammar.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — your paragraph, two words fixed

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — your paragraph, two words fixed
production_viz.mechanic: A handwritten-feel paragraph on cream. Exactly two words change — a comma and a verb tense — highlighted terracotta. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S10; it must be visually recognisable as the same object.

beats.narration_text: The obvious guess is that the mark is hidden characters — invisible spaces slipped between the words.

production_viz.label: Ghost characters between letters
production_viz.mechanic: Push in between two letters of a word; ghostly zero-width glyphs fade up in the gaps, drawn convincingly. Sell the wrong model.

beats.narration_text: If that were true, retyping the sentence by hand would strip it — and it doesn't, because there was never anything hidden to strip.

shot.new_visual_element: Retyped clean; the mark survives anyway

production_viz.label: Retyped clean; the mark survives anyway
production_viz.mechanic: The same sentence retypes character by character into a plain empty field. The ghost glyphs from S04 fail to appear. Then the terracotta underline from S01 sweeps the retyped line anyway — the mark survived.

beats.narration_text: Claude writes one word at a time, and very often several words would do equally well.

production_viz.label: Word-by-word, then a fork
production_viz.mechanic: A sentence builds left to right, one word at a time. At the final position the line forks into three equally weighted candidate words.

beats.narration_text: The weather today was cold and — overcast, or grey, and normally a random number settles it.

production_viz.label: Two branches, a die picks
production_viz.mechanic: The literal sentence 'The weather today was cold and' with two branches: OVERCAST and GREY. A die tumbles in and picks one. Both branches stay equally lit — neither is better.

beats.narration_text: Watermarking changes only where that randomness comes from: a key, plus the few words just before.

shot.new_visual_element: The die swapped for a key

production_viz.label: The die swapped for a key
production_viz.mechanic: The die is lifted out and replaced by a key, wired to the preceding few words. Same fork, same two branches — only the selector changed.

beats.narration_text: The choices still look random, but now the whole sequence can be checked against that key.

production_viz.label: Sequence checked against the key
production_viz.mechanic: A long row of past word-choices. The key sweeps across; each choice ticks as consistent. A confidence bar fills as the row lengthens — short row, weak; long row, strong.

beats.narration_text: Which is why that paragraph you only had proofread carries almost nothing — Claude chose a handful of words, and a handful is not a pattern.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — two words, no pattern

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — two words, no pattern
production_viz.mechanic: THE S03 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical. Only the two changed words light terracotta. The confidence bar from S09 appears beneath and barely moves.

beats.narration_text: And where only one answer is right — a name, a number, a line of code — there is no free choice to mark at all.

shot.new_visual_element: Forks that collapse to one branch

production_viz.label: Forks that collapse to one branch
production_viz.mechanic: Three forks in a column, each collapsing to a single branch: 'Principia ___' to MATHEMATICA, '2 + 2 =' to 4, and a line of code to its only valid token. No die, no key — nowhere for the mark to live.

beats.narration_text: So a mark found does not prove a human didn't write it — Claude may only have edited.

production_viz.label: Positive result, wrong conclusion struck
production_viz.mechanic: Left half: MARK FOUND, ticked. An arrow runs to the conclusion 'A HUMAN DIDN'T WRITE THIS' and that conclusion is struck through in terracotta.

beats.narration_text: And no mark found does not prove Claude wasn't there — too short, too factual, or too lightly touched.

production_viz.label: Negative result, wrong conclusion struck
production_viz.mechanic: Right half, mirroring S12: NO MARK, ticked. Arrow to 'CLAUDE WASN'T INVOLVED', struck through. Three small reasons fade in beneath: TOO SHORT, TOO FACTUAL, TOO LIGHTLY EDITED.

beats.narration_text: The watermark says Claude probably touched this text. It never says a human didn't write it.

props.quote: The watermark says Claude probably touched this text. It never says a human didn't write it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Take three paragraphs you wrote yourself, ask Claude to only fix grammar and punctuation, and count how many words actually changed. Then ask it to rewrite the same paragraphs freely, and count again. The gap between those two numbers is the watermark's resolution, on your own writing. Liam, in for Bear.
